clinic.method: I reused the reviewed fill method from docs/program/evidence/harness-bottlenecks/fill unchanged except for two edits. The four .js.txt files were copied to C:/Users/User/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/b6c3202ba5123743/05fc6dc4-8dea-4418-8b3c-6244e4758c7b/scratchpad/tokens/fill-clinic/ as fill.js, parse.js, run.js and summary.js. The method: context(k+1) - context(k) = output of call k + content that arrived between the calls. That growth is split by character share into categories, and each piece is weighted by how many later calls in the same window re-read it. A window breaks on a context drop of more than 20%. I ran run.js and then summary.js. I also added extra.js, a read-only pass over fill-result.json, because summary.js prints neither the per-category, per-kind (code/doc/data) and own-output splits nor the top-15 paths as shares. Printed summary, all groups: fetched 26.9%, own 31.1%, start 29.6%, unclassified 4.7%, messages 2.8%, rest 4.8%. Actual context tokens 5226M, attributed 5255M. Windows 522, distinct file paths 2750. The 30 most-read files are 6.7% of all tokens, and the 12 documents among them are 3.1%. Calls: slice-main 9327 (26 transcripts, 69 windows), root-main 2214 (15 transcripts, 20 windows), subagents 9646 (431 transcripts, 433 windows). The 'all' row's start of 29.6% splits into window-start 18.7% and window-start-after-compaction 10.89%. 'Rest' is everything else: harness-note 1.21, shell-run 1.03, tool-other 0.57, edit-confirm 0.54, connector 0.39, tool-schemas 0.32, harness-file-snippet 0.27, subagent-report 0.24, shell-git-write 0.22.
clinic.caveats: Edits made: (1) In fill.js, `dirs` keeps the original startsWith filter for the clinic prefix (19 folders: main + 18 worktrees). I appended the OneDrive store C--Users-User-OneDrive-Documents-Bilal-Migration-User-Downloads-20-PROJECTS-24-Clinic-Workshop, for 20 dirs in total. (2) In parse.js, the `nov` flag is set to `true` for every call (it was timestamp startsWith '2026-11'), so the run covers all time. Nothing else changed. run.js still groups by d.includes('worktrees'): the OneDrive store counts as root-main, and of its 363 jsonl files, 11 are main transcripts and 352 are subagents. summary.js still prints the label 'shares of November context tokens', but the figures are all-time. Assumptions checked: run.js does not use verify/remeasure/lib.js or its path-key normalisation. The path key is pathOf() in fill.js, which keeps the last two path segments, lowercased. Paths that share those two segments across worktrees or repos therefore merge into one hot-file key; with the worktrees that is intended. The parser treats every subagent file (any file below the store root) as isSub, so Workflow and Agent-tool subagents are pooled in 'subagents' and not split. Known biases carried over from the prior review (verify/check.txt), which still apply: the shell classifier stops at the first segment. Reads that start with a variable assignment or a for loop land in shell-other. Heredoc writes and sed -i count as shell-read. On November data this put fetched about 1.6 points low (28.5 corrected). 'Opened again' (6.3%) is mostly a different range of the same file, not exact re-reading. Thinking drops that are not compactions make attributed exceed actual: 100.56% overall, 101.1% root-main. The 2.16 chars-per-token rate only splits own output into its parts (it sets the thinking share), not the totals. Shares are of context tokens, not of cost.

fixflow.caveats: Edits: (1) In fill.js, line 6 `dirs` now lists the six FixFlow store folders explicitly, filtered by existsSync; all six exist. (2) In parse.js, the `nov` flag is set to true for every call (all-time mode). Nothing else in the attribution changed. (3) parse.js skips lines starting {"type":"api-request-blob or {"type":"file-history before the type check. This only saves time: those lines failed the type test after parsing anyway. (4) extra.js was added to report the splits; it is read-only. Script assumptions: summary.js's header still says 'November context tokens', but here it covers all time. Grouping uses d.includes('worktrees'), so the OneDrive 23-FixFlow store counts as root-main. That is correct, because it is not a worktree. run.js does not use the clinic-specific path-key normalisation in verify/remeasure/lib.js; I grepped and found no references. Hot-path keys come from fill.js pathOf (last two segments, lowercased). Because of that, the same file read under different path forms can split into separate rows, e.g. 'program/ship-plan-2026-11.md' (0.74%) and 'ship-plan-2026-11.md' (0.22%, a bare relative path). Scratchpad files from different sessions can also merge under one key. Corpus shape differs from clinic: only 14 main transcripts have calls (10 root, 4 slice), and subagents are 77.7% of tokens. That subagent share is why window-start dominates the overall figure (48.9%): each of the 1118 subagent windows re-reads its own prefix, and that prefix includes the task brief, so subagent messages-in is about 0. Chars per token is 1.97, against clinic 2.21. The corpus includes this orchestrating session (05fc6dc4), which was still in progress when measured. The shell classifier has the known biases from verify/check.txt M1: reads that start with a variable assignment or a for loop land in shell-other, and heredoc or sed -i writes count as shell-read. Here shell-other is 8.1% (13.7% in slice-main), so fetched content is probably understated by a point or two. The 7.0% 'opened again' is mostly a different range of the same file, not exact repeats, per the prior review. Shares are of context (input) tokens, not cost.

refute.overall:
The core numbers hold. Token totals, rates and the 1h/5m split are right: the harness's own costUSD reproduces within 0.1% for every model in the transcripts except Haiku, which is mostly missing from them. Role attribution is right. FixFlow main's 38.6% of cost on 8.2% of calls is real: 52% of main's cost is 1h Fable cache writes at roughly 400k context. The context histogram and the over-200k / over-400k shares are exact.

The derived tables are less reliable. Four reported figures are materially wrong:
- **Cost by token type:** average.cjs ignores 1h writes. The mean is cache write 40.8% / cache read 30.1% / output 29.1%, not 35.1 / 33.1 / 31.8.
- **Calls per prompt and cost per prompt:** injected text is counted as prompts, 2.5x too many in FixFlow and 4.7x in Clinic. The real figures are about 183 / 140 calls per prompt (mean about 162) and about $17 per prompt.
- **Lookup measures:** the shell-other bucket is mostly lookups hidden behind variable prefixes. Lookup-only calls are 57.9% of calls and 47.7% of context (not 46.5 / 36.9). Lookups are 85.5% of tool-result chars (not about 73.5%).
- **Prefix estimate:** chars/4 is wrong for this content, which runs about 2.83 chars per token. The prefix is about 60k tokens and about 15.9% of main context, not 42k and 11.2%.

The pooled column is mis-weighted (main's pooled share of context is 58.8%, not 54.0%). outputComposition sums to about 200%. The equal-weight mean hides two structurally opposite repos: FixFlow spends 60% on workflow agents and Clinic 66% on the main session. Report the per-repo columns as the primary result.

Smaller issues:
- The Clinic harness sum double-counts $106.79.
- About 3% of FixFlow spend is off-topic sessions.
- The live session is included.
- About 1% of spend (harness-internal Haiku) is missing from the transcripts.

cost.whatCostStateCovers:
The cost-state line is the harness's running cost accumulator for one process run of a session. In its own window it covers every API call the process made:
- main-thread calls
- Agent-tool subagents
- Workflow subagents
- calls that never appear as transcript assistant lines: Haiku web-search/WebFetch/title-style side calls (inputTokens with zero cache, plus webSearchRequests), compaction summarization calls, and other side queries on the main model (+1-5% cache read/output on the main model in sessions with compactions).

**Cache-read comparison.** Inside [startTime, last cost-state], cost-state's cacheReadInputTokens equals main + agent + workflow:
- subagent-only models match to the token: 701c sonnet/opus 1.000, 9c3f sonnet/opus exact, 3b82 sonnet 1.000, e24f haiku agent+workflow 1.000, 7f34 sonnet/opus-4-8 exact.
- main-plus-workflow models land at 1.004-1.012.
- It is never main-only: 2d44 is 2.79x main and 6c9a is 1.5x main.

**What it misses.** It is not a lifetime session total, because it is only written at save points: resume and exit, often as duplicate consecutive lines. Four gaps follow:
1. **Counter resets.** When a resumed session starts a new process without restoring state, startTime resets and the counter restarts at 0. Everything before startTime is lost: FixFlow $508.79, Clinic $510.02. This includes sessions whose only cost-state is $0 (FixFlow $159.65, Clinic $130.13).
2. **Unsaved runs.** Runs that ended without writing a cost-state (crash, killed app or window) are lost, and the next resume restores the stale earlier value. Examples: e24f restored $127.39 after $252.67 of spend; 7f34 counted +$92 against $320; 2d44 counted +$42 against $70. Net inside-window loss: FixFlow $252.74, Clinic $247.55.
3. **Spend after the last save:** FixFlow $27.63, Clinic $79.86.
4. **Sessions with no cost-state line:** FixFlow $39.67, Clinic $245.32.

**Duplication.** Forked sessions copy the parent's cost-state lines, so summing over sessions double-counts them (Clinic +$106.79, 186f2bac/3b820b0e).

**Reconciliation.**
- FixFlow: 1497.11 list = 39.67 no cost-state + 159.65 zero cost-state + 508.79 before reset + 761.37 inside windows + 27.63 after the last save. Cost-state sums to $508.63, which is the inside-window figure minus $252.74 of unsaved runs.
- Clinic, deduped by message id: 2408.64 = 245.32 + 130.13 + 510.02 + 1443.30 + 79.86. Cost-state deduped sums to $1195.75, which is inside minus $247.55. Adding the fork duplicate $106.79 gives the reported $1302.54.
cost.pricingComparison:
Cost-state prices at exactly the list rates in pricing.json. thinkingTokens is a subset of outputTokens and is not billed again. Web searches add $0.01 each.

**Rates checked to the cent on sessions where the 5m/1h cache-write split is complete:**
- fable-5-1: $37.52 = $37.52 (9c3f).
- fable-5-2: $63.24 = $63.24 (701c).
- opus-5-5: $30.58 and $6.11 exact.
- sonnet-5-5: $6.02 and $3.71 exact.

Where cost-state's split fields undercount (the split was added mid-session, or is absent in older versions), costUSD still matches with all cache writes at the model's actual TTL:
- 7f34 fable-5-1: $174.72 vs $174.73, with everything at the 1h rate.
- 7f34 opus-5-5: $70.15 = $70.15, with everything at the 5m rate.
- 6c9a opus: $115.03 vs a list of $113.64 for transcript tokens.

**Haiku and other models:**
- haiku-5-5: in 0.1 / out 0.5, plus searches. Checks: 186f $4.4854 = 11.44M×0.1 + 0.742M×0.5 + 297×$0.01; 9c3f $0.0235; 6c9a $0.0210. e24f is within $0.01, with a cache-write mix.
- haiku-4-5-20251001: $1/$5 plus searches ($4.9946).
- opus-4-8: $5 in / $25 out / $0.50 cache read / $6.25 cache write. It is missing from pricing.json, so the transcript totals priced its one call at $0 (about $0.40 understated).

So the gap between $509/$1303 and $1497/$2418 is a coverage gap, not a pricing difference.
cost.recommendedDollarFigure:
**Report the transcript-derived list-price totals, deduplicated by message.id:**
- **FixFlow: $1,497** (1,497.11; no duplicate rows).
- **Clinic: $2,409** (2,417.90 minus $9.26 of fork-copied main rows). Adding the unpriced opus-4-8 call gives about $2,409.

**Why:**
- Cost-state uses the same prices, so pricing is not in dispute.
- Cost-state covers only about 34% (FixFlow) and about 50% (Clinic) of the spend, because of counter resets, unsaved runs, post-save spend and sessions without cost-state lines. In Clinic it also double-counts a fork.
- The cost-state sums ($509 / $1,303) are hard lower bounds on billed usage and should not be reported as spend.

**Uncertainty bound:**
- The transcript misses calls never logged as assistant lines: Haiku web-search/fetch and side calls, plus compaction summaries.
- Where cost-state fully covers a window, these add 0.4-5% per session (701c +3.1%, 6c9a +1.2%, 186f/3b82 pair +5.4%, 2d44 Haiku +$4.99).
- Applying roughly +0.5% to +3% to all spend gives FixFlow $1,497 to about $1,545 and Clinic $2,409 to about $2,480. Best point estimates are about $1,510 and about $2,440.
- The 5m-vs-1h cache-write assumption for rows with no split, defaulted to 5m, could only raise the totals slightly.

**These are API list-price equivalents, not the user's actual billing.** Subscription plans are not billed per token.

cost.caveats:
- **Timestamps.** Cost-state lines have no timestamp of their own. The cut time used is the timestamp of the preceding line in the transcript, and is identical for back-to-back duplicate cost-state lines.
- **Unsaved runs are inferred.** "Unsaved run" is inferred from segment arithmetic: a cost-state delta far below the list spend between two saves, or a stale value restored. The exact trigger (crash, killed desktop app, a process that never reached its save hook) is not visible in the transcript.
- **5m/1h default.** Rows with cache writes but no 5m/1h split were priced at the 5m rate.
- **Invisible-call uplift.** The 0.5-3% figure is estimated from fully covered sessions only. Haiku web-search volume varies a lot by session (0 to $4.99), so the upper bound is approximate.
- **Fork handling.** Fork detection used an identical startTime and totalCostUSD. Only one fork pair was found (Clinic 186f2bac/3b820b0e); FixFlow has none.
- **Scope.** All figures are API list-price equivalents.
- **Unchanged inputs.** Upstream pricing.json and calls.jsonl were not modified.
